name: KY-012 active buzzer module
description: Active piezo buzzer module: a buzzer with a built-in oscillator that beeps at about 2.5 kHz (2500 ± 300 Hz, at least 85 dB) whenever 3.3–5 V DC is applied between its S and - pins. No tone generation or PWM needed: a GPIO high is on, low is off. The signal pin powers the buzzer directly (up to about 30 mA). Sold as: Joy-IT / Keyes KY-012 active piezo buzzer module (COM-KY012APB), 3-pin header S, (middle, not connected), -.
eli5: A little beeper: set the pin high and it beeps, set it low and it goes quiet.

pins.name: S
pins.description: Signal: high (3.3–5 V) = beep, low = silent. This pin also supplies the buzzer's current (up to about 30 mA).

pins.name: NC
pins.description: Middle pin, not connected on this module (leave unconnected)

buildNotes: Wire S to a GPIO and - to GND; leave the middle pin unconnected. There is no separate supply pin: the GPIO powers the buzzer.

Active buzzer: it makes its own ~2.5 kHz tone from DC. Just drive the pin high or low; PWM or tone() will not change the pitch much and only makes it crackle. For melodies use a passive buzzer (KY-006).

The buzzer draws up to about 30 mA from the GPIO. An ESP32 pin can supply this; a Raspberry Pi Pico or Raspberry Pi pin is rated for much less (about 12 mA / 16 mA), so it will be quieter and stresses the pin. For full volume, or at 5 V, switch it with an NPN transistor (e.g. 2N2222 + 1 kΩ base resistor) from the 5 V rail.
It is loud (85 dB at 10 cm). Peel off the 'remove seal after washing' sticker only if you want it even louder.
Some clone boards print different labels or put + in the middle; check the silkscreen before wiring.

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time

buzzer = Pin({S}, Pin.OUT, value=0)  # S high = beep (active buzzer)
while True:
    buzzer.value(1)
    print('BEEP ON')
    time.sleep(1)
    buzzer.value(0)
    print('BEEP OFF')
    time.sleep(2)
